## Problem 1

Created function. It is in `source/birthday_repeated.R`

### Run this function 10000 times for each group size between 2 and 50.
```{r}

source("source/birthday_repeated.R")

birthday_results_df =
  expand_grid(
    number_of_people = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    repeated = map_lgl(number_of_people, birthday_repeated)
  )

birthday_results_df

```

### For each group size, compute the probability that at least two people in the group will share a birthday by averaging across the 10000 simulation runs
```{r}
birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(number_of_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) 

```

### Plot showing the probability as a function of group size
```{r}
birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(number_of_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = number_of_people, y = prob_of_repeat)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()
```

This plot shows that the greater the group size, the higher the probability that two people in the group will share a birthday. There only needs to be about 23 people in the group for there to be a 50% chance that two people in the group will share a birthday.


## Problem 2

### Create a dataframe containing all file names
```{r}
study_df = 
  tibble(
files = list.files("data/data"))
```

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

source("source/file_import.R")

study_df = study_df |> 
  mutate(
    file_df = map(files, file_import)
    ) |> 
  unnest(file_df) |> 
    separate(col = files, into = c("arm", "study_id"), sep = "_") |> 
  mutate(
    arm = case_match(
      arm,
      "con" ~ "control",
      "exp" ~ "experimental"
    ),
    study_id = str_remove(study_id, "\\.csv")
  )

study_df

```

```{r}
study_df |> 
ggplot(aes(x = week, y = value, group = study_id, color = study_id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(~arm)
```
Those in the control arm have lower values on average compared to those in the experimental arm. While the values of those in the experimental arm tend to increase as the weeks go on, the values of those in the control arm tend to stay the same or decrease.
